prompts.betta-signs:
Use case: AI-illustrated visual guide that helps a beginner fishkeeper recognise what is wrong with their fish. Photorealistic educational aquarium illustration, NOT cartoons, icons, vector drawings, watercolor, plastic 3D renders or poster typography. Realistic underwater macro-photography aesthetic: anatomically believable fish, natural scales, translucent fins, restrained aquarium light, softly blurred dark teal planted-aquarium background. The key feature in each cell must be OBVIOUS to a novice at thumbnail size, while staying believable (no horror, no gore, no giant parasites). Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, watermarks, arrows or symbols anywhere in the image.
STRICT CONTACT SHEET for cropping into twelve separate pictures: exactly FOUR equal-width columns and THREE equal-height rows, twelve equal square cells covering the complete image edge to edge. No gutters, no borders, no outer margin. Every cell is its own separate scene with its own background. Nothing crosses a cell boundary; keep the whole subject inside the central 85 percent of its cell. Never put a cell's feature into another cell. Follow the exact row-major order below.
Every fish in this sheet is a BETTA (Siamese fighting fish, Betta splendens): exactly one betta per cell, never a different species, never two fish. Unless a close-up of the head is requested, show the whole betta in side view with its flowing fins. Vary the betta colors across cells as listed. Each betta is underwater in a home aquarium.
Row 1 column 1: dark navy-blue veiltail betta covered with many separate small WHITE salt-grain dots on body and fins (ich), each dot a distinct grain like sprinkled table salt.
Row 1 column 2: dark red betta with a very fine GOLD-RUST powdery dust over its back and fins (velvet), much finer than salt grains, like gold powder seen in side light; fins slightly clamped.
Row 1 column 3: turquoise-green betta with one localized fluffy WHITE COTTON-WOOL tuft of fine threads sticking out from a small wound on its flank (fungus / water mold).
Row 1 column 4: dark purple-black betta with a flat irregular PALE GREY-WHITE patch across its back just in front of the dorsal fin, like a saddle (columnaris); flat, no fluffy threads.
Row 2 column 1: royal-blue halfmoon betta with RAGGED, SHORTENED, ROTTING fin edges, uneven melted-looking tail edges with dark red-black margins (fin rot).
Row 2 column 2: pale pink-white (platinum) betta with one round OPEN RED SORE on its flank where scales are missing, a small red crater (bacterial ulcer).
Row 2 column 3: red-and-blue betta with a round SWOLLEN BELLY, scales still lying flat and smooth (bloat).
Row 2 column 4: close side view of a yellow-orange betta head with one eye clearly BULGING OUT like a marble, slightly cloudy (popeye / eye problem).
Row 3 column 1: blue-and-white marble (koi) betta with rough white-pink CAULIFLOWER-LIKE wart clusters on the edge of its tail fin (raised lumps).
Row 3 column 2: blue betta at the very top of the water, mouth breaking the surface GASPING for air, gill covers flared, a few bubbles; the water surface line visible across the top of the cell.
Row 3 column 3: orange-red betta FLOATING SIDEWAYS near the surface, body tilted over on its side, unable to stay level (swim bladder). Water surface visible.
Row 3 column 4: dull, faded dark-blue betta resting listlessly near the gravel bottom with FINS CLAMPED tightly against its body, no spots or wounds; looks fine but clearly not active.

These are TREATMENT STEP pictures for a home aquarium guide, shared by all kinds of fish. Use generic small tropical fish (for example an orange platy or neon tetras) when a fish appears. Equipment must be plain and unbranded: every bottle, box, kit or bag has a BLANK label with no writing at all. Human hands may appear (no faces). Clean, calm, well-lit home aquarium scenes; each cell one single clear action with an uncluttered background.
Row 1 column 1: a hand guiding a small fish in a soft green aquarium NET into a SMALL BARE HOSPITAL TANK that holds only a heater and an air stone.
Row 1 column 2: an aquarium WATER TEST KIT: a rack of small glass test tubes filled with differently colored liquid (yellow, green, blue, purple) beside a small blank dropper bottle.
Row 1 column 3: a PARTIAL WATER CHANGE: a siphon hose running from an aquarium down into a plain bucket, water flowing.
Row 1 column 4: a hand squeezing drops from a blank-labeled WATER CONDITIONER bottle into a bucket of fresh tap water.
Row 2 column 1: a blank-labeled MEDICINE BOTTLE with a dropper standing beside a small aquarium, a few drops of colored medicine diffusing in the tank water.
Row 2 column 2: a submersible AQUARIUM HEATER and a glass THERMOMETER (no numbers visible) inside an aquarium, warm glow, a fish swimming calmly.
Row 2 column 3: a spoon of coarse white AQUARIUM SALT crystals being stirred into a cup of tank water to dissolve, beside the aquarium.
Row 2 column 4: an AIR STONE on the aquarium floor releasing a strong column of fine bubbles up to a rippling surface.
Row 3 column 1: tweezers holding a small piece of thawed, skinned green PEA in the water in front of a fish (feeding a pea).
Row 3 column 2: a GRAVEL VACUUM tube pushed into the gravel lifting out debris and uneaten food pellets.
Row 3 column 3: a clear TANK DIVIDER panel separating two fish in one aquarium: a tiger barb (fin-nipper) on one side, a long-finned fish safely on the other.
Row 3 column 4: WATCH AND WAIT: one calm, healthy fish swimming normally in a clean, clear, softly lit planted aquarium; peaceful, nothing wrong.
